question.text: The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math> X-ray of molybdenum has wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>071</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>. If the energy of a molybdenum atom with a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> electron knocked out is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>keV</mi></math>, the energy of this atom when an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> electron is knocked out will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>keV</mi></math>.
